_comment: Single registry for every scraper. The three grouped workflows
Actions matrix from this file, so adding a source is ONE line here instead of
group: how the data is fetched -- api (JSON/REST/XML endpoints), html (markup
parsed from pages), browser (a real Chrome via seleniumbase/undetected).
Grouping matters because each technique wants a different timeout and a
different cron slot: API sources are cheap and can run often, HTML sources are
polite-limited by page fetches, browser sources need minutes of startup.
timeout: per-job timeout-minutes, lifted from scrape.yml where the job
persisted hundreds of rows over the WAN (see the glints comment there).
max_env: the env var that caps rows in one run (each scraper's Settings has its
own env prefix). Leave null when the source has no cap. Only used when a
workflow_dispatch input supplies max_jobs -- normal scheduled runs use the
enabled: false keeps a source out of the matrix until it is deliberately
switched on (Indeed is here because it drives a real Chrome and gets blocked).

sources.notes: remoteok.com/api - single JSON page, whole corpus in one request
reed.co.uk/api/1.0 - paginated search plus per-job detail calls
cupid.51job.com search API, 100 jobs per page
api.irantalent.com position search; the slowest write because each row is its own WAN insert
sitemap for discovery (XML) + candidateapi for detail JSON - Iran
RSS feed, not HTML - cheapest source we have
sitemap_index round-robin over country families, then 300-500 KB HTML pages; throttles us if hit too often
listing pages + detail pages; backfill through page 840 completed 2026-10-09
facet API for discovery, checknum.asp HTML for details - Israel
public-portal API lists ids, announcement pages carry the detail - Georgia
real Chrome via seleniumbase UC mode; needs browser setup on the runner and is the most blockable source, so it stays opt-in
